Experimental build — not yet validated for leak prevention on Android. Do not use for sensitive activity. Tor does not hide your logged-in X account identity.

Turn Tor ON for X
Android VPN settings (optional)

Tor ON routes only the associated X app through Tor. Other apps keep their normal connection. Tor OFF returns X to its normal connection. If the VPN tunnel disappears unexpectedly, X may connect directly.

Android allows one VPN per profile. Android may hide VPNs that exclude this app; accepting VPN permission can replace your existing VPN.

Always-on VPN and Block connections without VPN are optional Android settings. Blocking connections without VPN can also block other apps and keep X offline after Tor OFF. Piko Tor never changes these settings automatically.
Android settings detected: Always-on VPN %1$s; Block connections without VPN %2$s.
ON
OFF

Android VPN settings are optional. If Block connections without VPN is enabled manually, other apps can lose Internet access and X can remain offline after Tor OFF. Piko Tor does not change these settings.
Android is blocking connections without VPN. Other apps can lose Internet access, and Tor OFF may leave X offline. Change this optional setting in Android VPN settings if you want normal connections.
Another VPN is active

Piko Tor has not started or replaced your VPN. Android allows one VPN per profile. Keep your current VPN, or open Android VPN settings to choose which provider you want to use. Piko Tor does not send X through Tor while another provider is selected.
VPN permission changed before Piko Tor could start. Your selected VPN has not been replaced by this action. Check Android VPN settings before trying again.
Retry Tor / refresh circuits
Turn Tor OFF for X

Turn Tor OFF and close the VPN tunnel? X will use its normal connection and may reveal your public IP. If you manually enabled Block connections without VPN in Android, X can remain offline and other apps can stay blocked. This action does not change Android VPN settings.
Turn Tor OFF before changing the associated app.
Start the VPN first.
Android could not start the service. Check VPN consent and system settings. Protection is not verified.
Tor OFF — X uses its normal connection unless Android VPN settings block it.
Tor requested, but VPN unavailable. X may connect directly unless Android blocks connections without VPN.
Strict Private DNS is unsupported in this milestone. Tor paused; the tunnel is retained.
No underlying Internet network detected — tunnel retained.
X tunnel active — connecting to Tor. No direct fallback while the tunnel remains active.
Tor unavailable — tunnel retained, no direct fallback configured.
Tor reports ready; X tunnel active. Other apps use their normal connection unless Android VPN settings block them. If the tunnel disappears, X may connect directly.
